text: Extracellular ATP (eATP) binds directly to the lectin receptor-like kinase P2K1/DORN1 with nanomolar affinity to initiate purinergic signaling in Arabidopsis roots.
FERONIA forms a heteromeric receptor complex with P2K1 at the plasma membrane, acting as a mandatory scaffold for eATP-induced phosphorylation of downstream targets.
Apoplastic eATP accumulation triggers NADPH oxidase RBOHD activation, generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) that modulate cell wall expansion in root growth zones.
Extracellular ATP regulates root cell expansion in a calibrated biphasic manner, coordinated with nitric oxide and apoplastic redox homeostasis.
